newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on massive fund short covering.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on massive fund short covering.

text.p: Massive short covering by funds boosted CBOT corn futures to a higher close amid no major shift in fundamentals, traders said.
"They covered another 50 million bushels. They covered about 50 million Friday and more today," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Traders pointed out that funds were very short in the corn market before the release Friday of a bullish USDA 1996 production and U.S. 1996-97 U.S. ending stocks report.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report released January 6 bore that out.
The CFTC said as of December 31 non-commercials, including funds, were short corn by 268 million bushels and long by 67.3 million.

Traders said the fund buying which started early in the session and continued through the close touched off buy-stops as the March contract broke through second resistance at the $2.70 per bushel level. Satisfactory exports of U.S. corn also were cited. Monday's USDA weekly inspections of 37.967 million bushels were above expectations for 25 to 30 million bushels.
Corn closed two to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 3-1/2 at $2.70-3/4.
Traders said commercial hedge selling limited the rally in corn. ADM Investor Services and Cargill Inc each sold five million bushels of March, the traders said.
"There was hedge selling today. Massive fund short covering but hedge sales kept a lid on it," a trader said.

Prudential Securities bought 12.0 million bushels of March, Refco Inc bought five million bushels each of March, May and December, Rosenthal Collins bought four million March and R.J. O'Brien bought seven million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 53,000 contracts, above the 47,773 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 600 March $2.70 calls at 5-1/2 cents, ING Derivatives bought 400 March $2.70 calls at 5-1/2 cents and Term Commodities sold 400 March $2.70 calls at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 19,960 traded Monday.
